names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 26 mai, «Sfântul Apostol Alfeu».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 26 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Αλφαίος ο Απόστολος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 26. мај ст. ст., „Свети апостол Алфеј“ — Свети is not a rank and апостол is the `apostle` in `types`; the bare personal name is what is left. **Measured, and it is a fold of two told apart by the Prologue itself**: `foldchk.py` returns `[('alphaeus-martyr-10-may', 'sr')]` for «Алфеј», because **this same book keeps an «Алфеј» on its own Julian 10 May** — the martyr of the three brothers, whose `serbian` row a reader of this wave wrote off the Охридски пролог за 23.05.2026 — **and two commemorations on one calendar means two men**, which is exactly how this fold is told. So the identical string is stored a second time on purpose, and the two folders are kept apart by their days and their ranks, the 10 May man being `martyr` and this one `apostle`. **A third Alphaeus is already distinguished in this folder’s own life**, the brother of Alexander and Zosimas kept on 28 September, so the corpus now reads three men of the name and says so on each. **It is stored on this folder and not on `james-son-of-alphaeus`, although that folder’s Greek form «Ιάκωβος του Αλφαίου» carries the same name**, because the heading is this folder’s heading and a patronymic inside another saint’s name is not a form of this one. The Greek form here, «Αλφαίος», and the Romanian «Alfeu» are the same bare name.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 26 mai — «Sfântul Apostol Alfeu»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 26ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Αλφαίος ο Απόστολος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 26 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar keeps «Sfântul Apostol Alfeu» on, with the same bare name and the same rank. **The page does not know which Alphaeus he is and says so**: «Δεν υπάρχουν σαφή βιογραφικά του στοιχεία, γι' αυτό δεν μπορούμε να αποφανθούμε με βεβαιότητα ποιος Αλφαίος είναι» — and it then gives two answers, James the son of Alphaeus of the Twelve, brother of the Evangelist Matthew (16 Νοεμβρίου), on Nikodemos the Hagiorite's authority among others; or, which it calls the likelier, the Alphaeus or Cleopas who was husband of the Mary who was kinswoman of the Mother of God, and who lived with his wife and children working for the spreading of the Gospel. That is uncertainty about **who** he is and not about whether he existed, and the page carries no asterisk, so the row is written and the uncertainty is recorded rather than decided. Relics: «Απότμημα… βρίσκεται στην Ιερά Μονή Εσφιγμένου Αγίου Όρους». No hymn. Note that the same page's head is the ground on which saint.gr calls Abercius and Helen his son and daughter, and that both of those are upgraded here too.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 08.06.2026 (26. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети апостол Алфеј“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, on the same menologion 26/5 the Romanian and Greek rows already carry, and **two sentences long**. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23 to 26 May is. **THE BOOK ANSWERS, IN ONE LINE, THE QUESTION THE OTHER TWO CALENDARS REFUSE — AND NO `related` ROW IS WRITTEN ON THE STRENGTH OF IT.** doxologia prints the line and no life. saint.gr says in so many words that there are no clear biographical particulars and that **it cannot pronounce with certainty which Alphaeus is meant**, then sets out two answers: some, Nikodemos the Hagiorite among them, take him for the father of James of the Twelve and of the Evangelist Matthew; others — **and this, saint.gr says, is the likelier** — take him for the Alphaeus or Cleopas who was husband of the Mary who was a kinswoman of the Mother of God. **The Prologue takes the first answer and states it flatly**: „Отац двојице апостола из Дванаесторице и то: Јакова Алфејева и Матеја Јеванђелиста“ — the father of two apostles of the Twelve, namely James the son of Alphaeus and Matthew the Evangelist. **It gives no argument and does not mention the other answer.** **WHY NO ROW.** `james-son-of-alphaeus` and `matthew-the-apostle` are both in the corpus, and a fatherhood is a kinship the body narrates, which is ordinarily the test that owes a row. **But this folder already carries `abercius-martyr-26-may` and `helen-martyr-26-may` in `related` as his son and his daughter, off saint.gr’s Cleopas reading** — and the two readings cannot both be true of one man’s family. Adding two more sons would leave the folder asserting an incoherent household and would silently prefer this book over the Greek page’s own stated preference. `docs/CORPUS.md` §10 reserves both *that two entries are one person* and *a `related` row*, and `BRIEF.md` §3 says that where a reader is not sure he says so and writes nothing. **So both identifications are in the prose, named and unlinked, neither is chosen, and the four rows this would have produced are the author’s to write or to refuse. This is the open question of the day.** **`dates` UNTOUCHED**: the Prologue gives no year, and „Скончао је свој земаљски живот мирно“ — he ended his earthly life in peace — is the one thing it says of his end. **That is itself new**: doxologia says nothing at all of his death and saint.gr says nothing of it either, so a peaceful end is this book’s alone, and it belongs to whichever Alphaeus this book means. `types` untouched at `apostle`, which the heading corroborates. No `locations`, the entry naming no place. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
